label: late original-phase input h or 0 after w/t/k/v/s/n context
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at positions t>=3, mostly t=4-7 (the last few tokens before <DEL>). Never fires at t<3, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. It is token-selective: input h (47% of mass, 12x lift) and digit 0 (24%), with weaker firing on y, f, r, 1, g, x. Mostly on the first occurrence of that token. Whether it fires depends on the earlier prefix: it is much more likely when tokens like w, t, k, v, s, n appeared earlier (first_tok w gives 4.7x lift), and it is suppressed when the prefix has tokens like c, i, l, f. The strongest activations are h at t=5-6 after a prefix starting with w/k/t. The predicate (original phase, t>=3, input h or 0, at least one of w/t/k/v/s/n seen earlier) gets dev F1 about 0.49 and mass recall about 0.65. It misses the weaker y/f/r/g firings and has many false positives, because the prefix dependence looks graded rather than all-or-nothing.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: h, 0, y, f; t=7: h, 0, y, f; t=6: h, 0, y, f) and the first original token (most: w, t, k, v, o, 2; least: 1, f, 0, h); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
